### workspace events --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace events [--follow] [--json] [--types A,B] [--since CURSOR] [--name WS]

Read the event log ($HOME/.workspace-events.jsonl) and every agent daemon's
hook events ($HOME/.local/state/workspace/.events/<workspace>.jsonl) as one stream,
oldest first. Each line carries a cursor; pass it to --since to resume
after that line. Only files are read, so a slow reader never holds up a daemon.

Hook event types: tool_started, tool_finished, subagent_started, subagent_stopped, session_started, session_ended, prompt_submitted, agent_status.
tool_started and tool_finished carry input: the first line of a Bash command, a file
tool's path, a Grep or Glob pattern, a WebFetch URL; at most 300 bytes, with
control characters blanked and a trailing … when cut. Other tools have none.
Stream lines: follow_started (first, with a cursor) and gap (the cursor is older
than what is kept; the lines after its time follow).

Options:
        --follow                     Keep reading new lines until stopped (JSONL with --json)
        --json                       JSON: one line per event with --follow, else one {schema_version, ok, events, cursor} document
        --types A,B                  Only these types (repeatable, or comma-separated)
        --since CURSOR               Resume after the line that printed CURSOR
        --name WS                    Only this workspace's events (this workspace only; its worktree workspaces are not included)
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Without --since, --follow starts at the end of every file, and a plain read prints
what is kept: the current event log and each daemon's file and its rotated copy.

Examples:
  workspace events    # read everything kept so far, as text, oldest first
  workspace events --types session_started,session_ended    # which sessions started and ended
  workspace events --follow --json    # watch every workspace live from a program, one JSON line per event; runs until stopped
  workspace events --follow --json --since "$LAST_CURSOR"    # pick a follower up after a restart; LAST_CURSOR is the cursor of the last line it printed (every line has one); runs until stopped
  workspace events --follow --json --name myapp --types tool_finished    # follow the tool calls of one workspace; runs until stopped
--- stderr
--- end
